research_rationale: Blocked, not submitted. Merits as read: Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1946 sec. 4 (held, 60 Stat. 1095-1096, read in full) transfers the Social Security Board's functions to the Federal Security Administrator and states 'The Social Security Board is abolished.' Sec. 11 provides for winding up and sec. 12 transfers personnel, property and funds only as the Director of the Bureau of the Budget determines; the plan has no clause continuing outstanding presidential orders. Both EO 8399 permissions are keyed to the Board by name (officers and employees of the Board; 'upon recommendation of the Board'; appointment 'under the Social Security Board'; 'when the Board and the Administrator deem'), so on the abolition date they lose their object unless read as carried to the Administrator. On a carry-over reading the permissions would still end no later than the abolition of the Federal Security Agency and its Administrator (Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1953, not held), so EO 11408 (signed 1968-04-25, 33 FR 6459, held) is an upper bound, not a first end, on either reading. Why the kit cannot carry it: the dossier holds no record that contains the sec. 4 abolition sentence. The TERM records joined from this statute are TERM:EO:8399:c0cfd9c2254361a6@6e2b7a7718e215bc (chars 3687-4105, which quote the abolition of the United States Employees' Compensation Commission) and TERM:EO:8399:dd51d86d27d5ae90@6e2b7a7718e215bc (chars 6998-7226, the grant-in-aid coordination clause); both carry actor EO:8399 and mechanism own_terms_condition. Citing either as the end would mislabel a statutory end as an own-terms end and quote the wrong body. The only ACT-type record for EO 11408 is missing ('target provision not located: EO:11408'). The July 16, 1946 effective date appears only as the Statutes at Large marginal note ('Effective July 16, 1946'); the rule is in the Reorganization Act of 1945 (59 Stat. 613), not held.

research_rationale: Blocked, not submitted. Newly held: Pub. L. 91-224 sec. 110(a)-(b) (84 Stat. 113, read) renames the Federal Water Pollution Control Administration the Federal Water Quality Administration and deems references to it in any law, plan, regulation, document or paper to refer to the new name (April 3, 1970; a renaming, not an end). Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1970 (84 Stat. 2086-2089, read in full) sec. 6(a)(1) abolishes 'The Federal Water Quality Administration in the Department of the Interior', exclusive of any functions; sec. 2(a)(1) transfers its functions to the EPA Administrator; sec. 4 transfers personnel as the OMB Director determines; sec. 3 lets the Administrator assign functions within the Agency. The plan neither names nor transfers the Commissioner's office. Its marginal note says 'Effective December 2, 1970'; sec. 7 and 5 U.S.C. 906(a) (not held) tie the date to congressional session days, which cannot be computed from held text. Later events: EO 11587 (1971-03-15) substitutes 'Commissioner, Water Quality Office, Environmental Protection Agency' for the words in item (8); EO 11604 (1971-07-02) deletes item (8). Three readings fit the held texts: (A) the Interior Commissioner office ended with the Administration on 1970-12-02; (B) the placement carried to the EPA post and ended with EO 11604 on 1971-07-02; (C) the words were replaced on 1971-03-15. The plan creates a real earlier-end candidate (A) that the codif claim could not test. Why the kit cannot carry A or B: the dossier's TERM records for this plan are machine condition spans with actor EO:11293 and mechanism own_terms_condition; the sec. 6 span (TERM:EO:11293:6708c90773c52f4e@1bab1501d05db0b7, chars 13693-13831) quotes only 'Abolitions, (a) Subject to the provisions of this reorganization plan, the following, exclusive of any functions, are hereby abolished:' without the Administration named or any date. EO 11604 deletes item (8) by its words and cites no EO number, so the dossier has neither an ACT nor an ACTOR_TEXT record for it (only ACT:EO:11293>EO:11587 and >EO:11708 exist). Reading C is not coherent with 'a renaming is not an end', and I do not adopt it.

research_rationale: Blocked, not submitted. Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1968 (82 Stat. 1369-1370, read in full) sec. 1(a) transfers the functions of the Secretary of HUD under the Urban Mass Transportation Act of 1964 to the Secretary of Transportation, reserving to HUD the authority under secs. 6(a), 9 and 11 of that Act that primarily concern urban planning and part of the functions under secs. 3-5; sec. 3 creates an Urban Mass Transportation Administration in the Department of Transportation headed by an Administrator at Level III; sec. 5 transfers personnel and property as the Director of the Bureau of the Budget determines; sec. 6 makes the plan effective at the close of June 30, 1968 or the 5 U.S.C. 906(a) time, whichever is later (marginal note: 'Effective June 30, 1968'). The plan does not mention the HUD Urban Transportation Administration or its Director and abolishes nothing in HUD. Whether that HUD office and the Director post ended on June 30, 1968, later, or only with EO 11634's deletion of item (8) on 1971-12-06 (an upper bound only, and not an ACT record because it names no EO number) is a matter for the HUD organization record, which was not found. The brief allows submission only if the held plan alone decides the clause; it does not. The dossier's clause inventory for EO 11299 is also wrong (24 draft clauses, 1 real: item (9) at chars 925-1023 of the held text; the rest are neighbouring Civil Service Commission regulations on the same Federal Register pages), so a corrected-inventory override would be needed in any case.

research_rationale: EO 11367 (signed 1967-08-18, 32 FR 12037; held official Federal Register text read in full) adds item (5), 'Assistant Director for Executive Management, Bureau of the Budget, Executive Office of the President', to section 1 (level IV) of EO 11248. It has one operative sentence, a standing pay-level designation under 5 U.S.C. 5317, with no term or condition. The rest of the held extract (migratory-bird and other regulations on the same pages) is neighbouring material, not part of the order. Newly held: Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1970 (84 Stat. 2085-2086, read in full). Sec. 102(a) provides 'The Bureau of the Budget in the Executive Office of the President is hereby designated as the Office of Management and Budget'; sec. 102(b) designates the statutory Assistant Directors (31 U.S.C. 16a, 16c) Assistant Directors of OMB; sec. 103 makes the Bureau's records, property and personnel OMB's. That is a redesignation of the same entity and offices, so it abolishes nothing and is not an end. The Statutes at Large marginal note gives 'Effective July 1, 1970' for the plan, and sec. 301 sets July 1, 1970 as the floor; no end date in this claim depends on that note. EO 11540 (signed 1970-07-01, 35 FR 10735; held, read in full) states 'This order shall be effective July 1, 1970' and substitutes, in item (5), 'Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget, Executive Office of the President' for the words of this order. I treat that as a conforming retitle, recorded as a later event and not as the first end: the item keeps its number and level IV, and the substituted title covers every OMB Assistant Director, including any post that was the former Assistant Director for Executive Management, so the placement was widened and renamed, not withdrawn. The dossier has no OMB organization record (the request was answered with the plan only); the judgment does not need one because the retitled item has a live object under sec. 102(b). The first end is EO 11708 (signed 1973-03-23, 38 FR 7979; held, read in full), sec. 3: 'Except with respect to the positions enumerated in section 2 of this order, Executive Order No. 11248 of October 10, 1965, as amended, is hereby revoked.' EO 11708 states no effective date or delay, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1973-03-23. Sec. 2 continues only eight level V positions, none of them OMB, so item (5) (level IV) is revoked; sec. 1(9) of EO 11708 places 'Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget' in level IV under its own authority, a new placement and not a residue of this order. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR disposition catalog: hits read, all EO 11540/11708) carry no coverage warning. A reviewer should test (a) whether EO 11540's substitution should be the first end instead (1970-07-01), and (b) whether the revocation date 1973-03-23 is right given EO 11708 has no effective-date wording.
savings_reason: Read EO 11708 secs. 1-3 and EO 11540 in full for saving, transition or incumbent-protection wording about item (5): none. EO 11708 sec. 3's only exception is the sec. 2 list of eight level V positions. EO 11367 created no office, fund, duty or vested right; it only designated a pay level for an existing office, and pay received while it stood is a completed consequence. EO 11708 sec. 1(9) re-places the OMB Assistant Director in level IV under its own authority, so no independent residual of EO 11367 remains.
earlier_end_check: Tested every instrument that could have ended or altered item (5) before 1973-03-23. (a) Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1970 (held, read in full): sec. 102(a) designates the Bureau of the Budget itself as OMB, sec. 102(b) redesignates the statutory Assistant Director offices, sec. 103 transfers its personnel to OMB; nothing is abolished, so no statutory end. (b) EO 11540 (held, effective July 1, 1970 by its own sentence): retitles item (5); treated as a later event, not an end, for the coverage reason given in the rationale. (c) I read the operative paragraphs of every other amender of EO 11248 issued after 1967-08-18 (EO 11369, 11384, 11385, 11389, 11393, 11400, 11409, 11416, 11421, 11441, 11463, 11468, 11489, 11499, 11504, 11510, 11516, 11542, 11550, 11581, 11587, 11604, 11634, 11641, 11676, 11699). None deletes, replaces or renumbers section 1 item (5): EO 11385 added item (6); EO 11389 added item (7); EO 11581 deleted item (6) and renumbered (7)-(11), leaving (5); EO 11409, 11441, 11468, 11489, 11604, 11634, 11641, 11676 and 11699 touch other section 1 items; the rest concern section 2 (level V). (d) No own-term, sunset or self-termination: the order is a single placement. (e) The OFR disposition catalog hits and the 1989 table point only to EO 11540 and EO 11708. The first end found is EO 11708 sec. 3.
scope_check: The first end is the revocation of the parent order EO 11248 as amended; the machine record marks scope 'partial' because of the exception for the sec. 2 positions. I read sec. 2 of EO 11708: it continues eight level V positions (Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense (Comptroller); Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Reserve Affairs; Assistant Secretary, Comptroller, HEW; Deputy Commissioner of Social Security; Commissioner on Aging; Deputy Director, Secret Service; Commissioner, Property Management and Disposal Service, GSA; Deputy Assistant Secretary for Model Cities, HUD). None is item (5), and item (5) is a section 1 (level IV) item while sec. 2 continues only level V positions, so the revocation reaches this clause in full. The whole order is this one item, so the whole-order end is the clause end.
independent_command_check: The order contains one operative sentence, an amendment adding item (5) to EO 11248 sec. 1. The only continuing effect is the level IV designation under 5 U.S.C. 5317. It imposes no duty on any officer, no report, no fixed term and no condition, and it is a standing designation, not a performed command, so it lasted until altered or revoked. No independent command survives the revocation.

Transferred or accrued effects: none; the level IV placement of the OMB Assistant Director is re-made by EO 11708 sec. 1(9) under that order's own authority, which is that order's provision, not a residue of EO 11367.
